title:	[Bug]: Model switch to unresponsive Ollama model cascades into infinite [object Object] loop, corrupts session
state:	OPEN
author:	fgomsan
labels:	bug, bug:crash

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Description

Switching the primary model via chat to a local Ollama model that doesn't respond 
(ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:122b) caused a cascading failure that made the entire system 
unusable — all responses on all surfaces (Telegram, webchat) became `[object Object]`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Running OpenClaw v2026.3.28 with Claude Opus as primary model
2. Switch model to a local Ollama endpoint (122B MoE model) via `/model` command
3. Model fails to respond (likely memory/speed constraints on DGX Spark)
4. Session enters corrupted state

## What Happens

1. Model switch hangs — no graceful timeout or fallback to previous model
2. Session transcript grows beyond context window (434K tokens vs 200K limit)
3. Compaction triggers in a loop, injecting internal messages 
   ("Pre-compaction memory flush...") into the Telegram channel as user-visible messages
4. Agent responds to internal compaction messages with `NO_REPLY`
5. `NO_REPLY` is serialized as `[object Object]` and sent to Telegram
6. This creates an infinite loop: [object Object] → compaction → internal msg → NO_REPLY → [object Object]
7. Even switching back to Claude doesn't fix it — session is permanently corrupted

## Expected Behavior

- Model switch should have a timeout (e.g., 30s). If model doesn't respond, 
  revert to previous model with a user-visible error message
- Internal compaction messages should NEVER be sent to chat channels
- `NO_REPLY` should never be serialized as `[object Object]`
- Session corruption should not require full `openclaw reset` to recover

## Recovery Required

Had to: kill gateway, move inflated transcript to .bak, run `openclaw doctor`, 
run `openclaw reset` (config+credentials+sessions), restore openclaw.json from backup.
~1 hour of downtime.

## Environment

- OpenClaw v2026.3.28
- macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), Mac Mini M4 Pro 64GB
- Primary: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
- Failed model: ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:122b (Ollama on DGX Spark, 119GB RAM)
- Channels: Telegram + webchat

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to Reproduce:

1. OpenClaw v2026.3.28, primary model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (200K context)
2. Switch model via chat to a local Ollama endpoint that fails to respond (e.g. ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:122b — large MoE model on constrained hardware)
3. Model hangs — no timeout, no fallback to previous model
4. Session transcript inflates beyond context window (434K tokens vs 200K limit)
5. Compaction triggers in a loop, injecting internal messages ("Pre-compaction memory flush...") into the Telegram channel as user-visible messages
6. Agent responds with NO_REPLY, which gets serialized as [object Object]
7. Infinite loop: [object Object] → compaction → internal msg → NO_REPLY → [object Object]
8. All responses on all surfaces (Telegram + webchat) are now [object Object]
9. Even switching back to Claude doesn't fix it — session is permanently corrupted
10. Recovery requires: kill gateway, remove inflated transcript, openclaw reset (config+sessions)

### Expected behavior

1. Model switch should have a configurable timeout (e.g. 30s). If the model doesn't respond, revert to the previous model with a user-visible error message like "Model X did not respond, reverting to Y"
2. Internal compaction messages ("Pre-compaction memory flush...") should NEVER be sent to chat channels (Telegram, webchat, etc.) — they are internal housekeeping, not user-facing content
3. NO_REPLY sentinel should never be serialized as [object Object] — it should either be suppressed or rendered as empty
4. A single model failure should not be able to corrupt the entire session beyond recovery
5. Recovery from a bad model switch should not require full openclaw reset + manual transcript removal — a simple /model switch back or gateway restart should suffice

### Actual behavior

1. Model switch to unresponsive Ollama model hangs indefinitely — no timeout, no fallback
2. Session transcript grows unchecked to 434,828 tokens (over the 200K context limit)
3. Compaction triggers repeatedly in a loop, injecting internal system messages into the Telegram chat as if they were user-facing responses
4. Agent responds to these internal messages with NO_REPLY, which is serialized and sent to Telegram as [object Object]
5. This creates an infinite feedback loop: [object Object] → triggers compaction → internal message sent to chat → NO_REPLY → [object Object] again
6. ALL responses on ALL surfaces (Telegram and webchat) become [object Object] — the bot is completely unusable
7. Switching back to the original model (Claude) does NOT fix it — the session remains corrupted
8. Only way to recover: kill gateway process, manually remove the inflated session transcript (.jsonl), run openclaw doctor + openclaw reset with scope config+sessions, restore openclaw.json from backup. ~1 hour downtime.

### OpenClaw version

2026.3.28

### Operating system

26.3.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm (pnpm)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (primary, API key auth)

### Provider / routing chain

• Primary: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (cacheRetention: "long") • Subagents primary: ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:35b-a3b (DGX Spark local) • Subagents fallbacks: ollama-dgx/nemotron-cascade-2 → ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:122b → ollama/qwen3.5:27b → google/gemini-2.5-flash • Heartbeat: google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview • Crons: various (isolated sessions)

### Additional provider/model setup details

• anthropic: API key, default profile
• ollama: local Mac Mini (127.0.0.1:11434), models: qwen3.5:27b, qwen2.5:32b, llama3.3
• ollama-dgx: DGX Spark (192.168.1.112:11434), models: qwen3.5:35b-a3b, qwen3.5:122b, nemotron-3-super, nemotron-cascade-2
• google: Gemini API (generativelanguage.googleapis.com)
• xai: Grok API (api.x.ai)
• openrouter: nemotron free tier

The crash was triggered when switching the main session model from anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 to ollama-dgx/qwen3.5:122b via chat command. The 122b model (81GB, MoE) likely failed to load or respond within the DGX's constraints.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

```shell
nfortunately the corrupted session transcript (58b95468-a66e-4ccd-ae18-abe22694490c.jsonl, 12.7MB, 434,828 tokens) was moved to .bak and subsequently cleaned up during the openclaw reset process, so the raw log is no longer available.

Key evidence from troubleshooting (performed via Claude.ai while the system was down):

1. Session transcript had grown to 12.7MB / 434,828 tokens (over 2x the 200K context limit)
2. Gateway process (PID 7493, then 8046) had to be force-killed
3. All Telegram messages from the bot showed literal "[object Object]" text
4. Webchat (dashboard) showed the same [object Object] output
5. openclaw doctor found and archived 37 orphaned transcripts during recovery
6. Current gateway log shows compaction safeguard triggering: "no real conversation messages to summarize; writing compaction boundary to suppress re-trigger loop" — evidence of the loop protection kicking in on the fresh session

The [object Object] serialization bug suggests a JS object is being passed to the message renderer where a string is expected — likely the NO_REPLY sentinel or an internal compaction message object being sent without .toString() or proper serialization.
```

### Impact and severity

Severity: Critical / P1

• Complete system outage: ALL responses on ALL channels (Telegram + webchat) became [object Object] — the bot was 100% unusable
• No self-recovery: the system could not recover on its own, nor via simple gateway restart or model switch-back
• Data loss: session history and context lost during forced reset
• Manual intervention required: ~1 hour of troubleshooting from an external Claude.ai session (the bot itself couldn't help since it was broken)
• Recovery procedure is non-trivial: kill process, remove transcript, openclaw doctor, openclaw reset, restore config from backup — not something a typical user would figure out easily
• Root cause is a common user action: switching models via /model command should be a safe, reversible operation
• Cascading failure: a single model timeout escalated into session corruption, infinite loops, and total service loss with no circuit breaker at any stage

### Additional information

Suggested fixes (in order of priority):

1. Model switch timeout + automatic rollback: If a new model doesn't respond within N seconds (configurable, default 30s), revert to previous model and notify the user. This alone would have prevented the entire incident.
2. Guard against sending internal messages to chat channels: Compaction messages, memory flush notifications, and other internal housekeeping should never reach Telegram/webchat/Discord. They should be filtered at the message rendering layer.
3. NO_REPLY serialization guard: Ensure NO_REPLY sentinel is always handled as a string suppression signal, never passed as an object to channel renderers. A simple typeof check before sending would prevent [object Object].
4. Transcript size circuit breaker: If a session transcript exceeds the model's context window, halt processing and alert the user rather than entering a compaction loop. Consider auto-archiving the session and starting fresh.
5. Easier recovery path: A command like "openclaw sessions reset --agent main" that clears the corrupted session without requiring full config+credentials reset would make recovery much faster.

Config at time of crash:

• compaction.mode: "safeguard"
• compaction.recentTurnsPreserve: 6
• contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl" (ttl: "4h")
• bootstrapMaxChars: 12000 (AGENTS.md 18,824 chars + MEMORY.md 20,438 chars were both being truncated every turn, which may have contributed to the rapid transcript inflation)
